title: Listen to the Latest ‘KFF Health News Minute’
summary: The "KFF Health News Minute" brings original healthcare and health policy reporting from our newsroom to the airwaves each week.

title: Midterm Voters Split on Abortion and Trans Healthcare Ballot Questions
summary: The nationwide blue wave in the midterm election didn’t necessarily carry over to ballot measures on abortion and transgender issues.

title: Trump Administration Delays Awards Slated To Improve Rural America’s Health
summary: State leaders who scrambled to win and begin spending their first-year shares of Republicans’ five-year, $50 billion fund are in the dark about how much they’ll receive in the Rural Health Transformation Program’s second year after a federal office notified states that more time is needed to make allocations.

title: Democrats’ Election Rout Is Poised To Dramatically Reorder Federal Health Policy
summary: Democrats’ retaking of Congress doesn’t change President Donald Trump’s control of the veto pen — making the new majority’s aspirations to reverse changes to Medicaid, the Affordable Care Act, and other safety net programs an uphill climb.

title: IVF Patients, Doctors Navigate Fetal Personhood Laws’ Unknowns
summary: People trying to start families and clinics trying to help them have been left confused and worried since the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, triggering fetal personhood laws in several states.

title: Stuck in Shelters for Months, Some Migrant Children Abandon Hopes of Staying in US
summary: The federal Office of Refugee Resettlement is supposed to care for migrant children who arrive in the country alone. But new policies are stranding kids in shelters and undermining their mental health. Some children have chosen to return to the countries they fled.

title: A Few Miles From the US Capitol, Dozens Slept in Their Cars, Waiting for Free Care
summary: If you’ve heard about how people are struggling with affording healthcare but haven’t been touched by it or seen it, then this pop-up clinic just outside Washington, D.C., put the problem on full display.

title: Expecting a Baby? Five Tips To Help You Prepare for Pregnancy Costs
summary: The cost of having a baby is frustratingly difficult to predict. The actual amount families pay varies widely. Here are five tips to help you prepare for the often-unexpected costs of pregnancy and giving birth.

title: A GOP Congressman Backed Medicaid Work Requirements. His Voters Might Be Exempt.
summary: A California congressman voted for the GOP’s One Big Beautiful Bill, which is projected to reduce Medicaid spending by $900 billion. Now Rep. David Valadao, whose House race will help decide control of Congress, is telling his constituents they may not have to follow the new rules.

title: Georgia Helped Inspire the Medicaid Work Rules. Its Own Rules Could Soon End.
summary: For years, Georgia was the only state to require some Medicaid enrollees to work to obtain and keep coverage. Those rules could expire just as the federal Medicaid work requirements they helped inspire roll out across most of the country.
